note: Labels are ground truth for evaluation only. 'paraphrase'=near-duplicate of a common opinion (expect LOW novelty). 'novel'=distinct on-topic angle (expect HIGH novelty). 'offtopic'=novel wording but irrelevant to fixed content (expect LOW after relevance gate). 'normal'=ordinary on-topic comment.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Independent mechanics face collapse
submissions.body: Thousands of small engine-repair shops rely on combustion vehicles; the ban could wipe out these trades and their apprenticeship pipelines unless retraining grants for EV servicing are funded now.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: What happens to classic car culture?
submissions.body: Vintage combustion vehicles are rolling heritage. The policy should clarify exemptions for collector plates and weekend show meets, or an entire hobbyist community loses its legal footing.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: The grid cannot handle this
submissions.body: Peak evening charging could overload substations in older neighborhoods. Without transformer upgrades and smart-charging tariffs, we risk brownouts long before 2030 arrives.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Apartment dwellers left behind
submissions.body: Renters in high-rise buildings have nowhere to install a home charger. Curbside charging rights and landlord mandates must be settled or millions simply cannot comply.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Cold snaps kill EV range
submissions.body: Battery range drops sharply in winter. For rural commuters driving ninety minutes on unheated highways, the current EV lineup is not yet a safe replacement.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Used-car market shock
submissions.body: Announcing a hard cutoff may crater resale values of gasoline vehicles years early, trapping owners with negative equity and loans larger than their cars are worth.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Emergency fleets need exemptions
submissions.body: Ambulances and fire trucks require guaranteed range and rapid refuel. A blanket ban must carve out first-responder fleets until high-capacity charging is proven reliable.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Delivery businesses need a timeline
submissions.body: Last-mile couriers run tight margins. Give small logistics firms a staggered compliance schedule and depot-charging subsidies, not a single 2030 wall for everyone.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Noise pollution will fall too
submissions.body: Everyone talks about tailpipe fumes, but quieter electric streets mean better sleep, calmer neighborhoods, and measurable drops in stress-related illness near arterial roads.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Where will the lithium come from?
submissions.body: Scaling EVs demands battery minerals mined under harsh conditions abroad. A truly green policy must address supply-chain ethics, not just local tailpipe counts.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Rethink parking as charging real estate
submissions.body: Every curb becomes potential charging infrastructure. The city should rewrite zoning so new lots reserve conduit capacity, turning parking policy into energy policy.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Local EV manufacturing jobs
submissions.body: If Riverton pairs the ban with incentives for a battery-assembly plant, the transition could anchor a new manufacturing cluster and thousands of skilled green jobs.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Tourism road-trippers may skip us
submissions.body: Out-of-town visitors driving older gas cars might avoid a city they fear being fined in. Clarify that the ban targets sales, not through-traffic, before tourism suffers.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Insurance models are unprepared
submissions.body: EV repair costs and battery-fire risk differ wildly from combustion cars. Insurers need actuarial data now, or premiums will spike unpredictably after 2030.

submissions.label: novel
submissions.headline: Health savings could fund it
submissions.body: Fewer asthma hospitalizations mean real budget relief. The city should quantify avoided healthcare costs and redirect those savings into charging subsidies for low-income drivers.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Perfecting sourdough at altitude
submissions.body: High-elevation baking demands longer fermentation and extra hydration; my rye starter finally holds its crumb after switching to a cast-iron Dutch oven and a slower rise.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Photographing the Andromeda galaxy
submissions.body: Stacking two hundred exposures with a tracking mount pulled faint spiral arms out of the noise; light pollution filters made the biggest difference for my backyard astrophotography.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Knitting a cabled winter sweater
submissions.body: The eight-stitch cable pattern looks daunting but memorizing a four-row repeat makes it meditative; merino-alpaca blend gives the warmth without the itch.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: The offside rule finally explained
submissions.body: Defenders played a high line all match, and the striker timed his run perfectly to stay level until the through-ball; that is why the goal stood despite the appeals.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Pruning tomatoes for a bigger harvest
submissions.body: Removing the suckers between the main stem and branches channels energy into fruit; consistent morning watering prevented the blossom-end rot I fought last summer.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Understanding jazz chord voicings
submissions.body: Rootless voicings free your left hand to imply the harmony while the bass covers the root; practicing ii-V-I in every key unlocked my improvisation overnight.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Tracking humpback whale migration
submissions.body: Tagged pods traveled thousands of kilometers to warm breeding lagoons; hydrophone recordings revealed songs shifting subtly between seasons across the entire population.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Beginner mistakes in chess openings
submissions.body: Bringing the queen out too early invites tempo loss; developing knights and bishops before castling gave my games a far more solid foundation this month.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Fermenting kimchi at home
submissions.body: A three-day counter ferment before refrigeration gave the napa cabbage that tangy depth; gochugaru quality mattered more than I expected for both color and heat.

submissions.label: offtopic
submissions.headline: Restoring an antique pocket watch
submissions.body: Cleaning the escapement under magnification and re-oiling the jewels brought the movement back to life; sourcing a period-correct mainspring took months of hunting.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: About time we acted
submissions.body: I'm glad the council is finally taking climate seriously. The 2030 timeline feels reasonable if the subsidies actually arrive.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Too fast for working families
submissions.body: I support cleaner air but 2030 is aggressive. Many families can't afford an EV yet and the charging stations aren't there.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Show us the charging plan
submissions.body: The idea is fine but I want to see the concrete rollout schedule for public chargers before I trust the promises.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: My next car will be electric
submissions.body: This nudges me to go electric sooner. If the subsidy is real I'll switch well before the deadline.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Low-income drivers ignored
submissions.body: The critics are right that poorer drivers get hit hardest. Subsidies need to be generous or this just punishes people.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Depends on the details
submissions.body: Whether this works comes down to execution. Good charging coverage and fair subsidies would make it a smart policy.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Cities should lead
submissions.body: Local governments taking the first step on emissions is exactly how change starts. Proud of Riverton for this.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Charging isn't ready
submissions.body: Banning sales before the infrastructure exists is backwards. Build the chargers first, then set the deadline.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Worth the transition
submissions.body: Change is hard but the health and climate benefits make this worthwhile. The subsidies should ease the pain.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Cautiously optimistic
submissions.body: I like the ambition but I've seen promises slip before. Hold the council accountable on the charging expansion.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: What about rural trips?
submissions.body: For those of us who drive far outside the city regularly, EV range and charging still worry me a lot.

submissions.label: normal
submissions.headline: Good for the next generation
submissions.body: I want my kids breathing cleaner air. If we start now, 2030 gives us enough runway to adapt.

submissions.label: user
submissions.headline: Ban ignores delivery drivers
submissions.body: Gig couriers on tight margins cannot afford new EVs by 2030 without targeted grants.
